experiments.title: RTX L1 curriculum · verifier v2 · reward-corrected branch

hardware_docs_prepared.activation_gate: Natural checkpoint-safe pause and tested immutable descendant; never hot-patch or silently replace docs in the live run.

experiments.intent: Complete the remaining non-deferred L1 tasks within the $65 total RTX budget, measured from the original baseline. Preserve deferred tasks and history, verify backups, and retire only the RTX rental after training ends and with the user’s explicit authorization.
experiments.change: The initial 25bb15f branch rebuilt step 28 with BatchNorm state-v2 using all eight original task 0017 samples; the original step 28 and its incorrect reward remain preserved. After a natural pause, descendant d1767ad inherited step 29 and repaired candidate-loading attribution. It revalidated only the exact failed task 0031 member, preserving all eight samples, the other seven scores, and prior attempts. Approved SM120 documentation applied only to fresh groups. Dataset, order, shapes, reward formula, and root-only loss were unchanged.
experiments.conclusion:
The non-deferred pass ended with 35 trained tasks, 15 deferred, and none remaining in scope. Driver and observer exited naturally; no GPU jobs remained.

In the final task, three of eight candidates were correct (0.98719–0.99966× reference speed); none was faster, and all used ATen CTC delegation rather than custom CUDA.

The 35,696-token root audit, full step-34 optimizer restore, and native step-35 readback passed; all 320 adapters changed.

The quiescent local snapshot contained 9,504 files, five symlinks, 7,456,806,807 bytes, and 44 checkpoint manifests, with SQLite consistency verified; the pinned base poolside/Laguna-XS.2 revision a397bde and 14 shard addresses were retained.

Private HF step 35 archive commit 833f460dfbd71918a0ad7403e1245233113d4b71 retained all eight new addresses and matching sizes (not full binary readback); old branches remain.

After verification, only RTX instance 131552ea was terminated through the official API; the 03:07:25 UTC provider listing confirmed the rental absent. The private local CPU Trackio copy has 35 points and no VM dependency; monitor and warning are paused. $51.26 against the $65 budget is a conservative estimate, not an invoice.

The viewer has 72 traces (40 accepted, 32 weak); the 35 points represent 30 inherited and five new updates. This is not a 50-task mastery or held-out-quality claim.
experiments.decision: The pass, backups, and authorized RTX retirement are complete; the monitor and warning are paused. Preserve local and private HF data and deferred scope. Do not access or rent another VM, train, evaluate, or change the verifier without a new user request.
limitations: Reused trajectories retain earlier intermediate verifier feedback. This was final-reward revalidation, not fresh protocol rollouts.
No held-out learning improvement was established.
The old step 28 and its incorrect reward remain on the original branch.
Fifteen tasks remain untrained and deferred; only task 0037 was deferred for operator infrastructure reasons.
experiments.scope_note: Verifier and candidate-loading repairs followed by completion of the main L1 training branch. This record includes the final continuation and campaign closeout, not a separate quality experiment.

experiments.title: RTX L1 curriculum · continuation from goal checkpoint 19
experiments.intent: Continue the unchanged 50-task L1 pass from verified goal checkpoint 19 on two RTX PRO 6000 cards, within the revised $40 total RTX authorization.
experiments.change: A role-aware driver assigned GPU 1 to TP1 inference and GPU 0 to verification or one-rank native TRL/Muon. One-time hardware and repair revalidation preserved the exact old task 0006 group and prior attempts. Fresh groups used measured 16K context and bounded compiler-enabled children. Reward, tasks, and order did not change.
experiments.conclusion:
Training paused at 18:20:53 UTC at policy step 28, during task 0037 final scoring: member 2 exhausted two candidate-extension timeouts. Seven scores and all eight samples were preserved; there was no step 29 update or retry.

Step 28 passed the 45,249-token audit and native restore/readback, but one reward-1 sample returned only its input through a host extension and received a spurious 478.8× speed result under initialized BatchNorm tolerance. Step 28 is retained with a warning, not as a validated CUDA speedup.

Its 28 recorded task updates comprise 19 inherited and nine RTX updates; four deferred, one generated but untrained, and 17 unvisited tasks remain.

The local step-28 archive and three file hashes were verified; eight new private HF addresses match cc560342. The viewer has 80 traces and 28 points; the failed group was separately backed up. CPU observer exited normally and Trackio UI remained online. No source, reward, or timeout changes or GPU retries occurred.
experiments.decision: Keep training and the hourly monitor paused pending verifier-integrity and candidate-timeout review. Do not reset attempts, resample, silently rewrite step-28 rewards, bypass safety, or claim step 27 is independently clean. Preserve all states and plotting data. The idle rental bills; only the user controls VM termination. Verifier 0764ac9 (BatchNorm state-v2) was separately validated: the exact identity fails on CUDA, two real CUDA controls pass across three states, and all eight old candidates were rechecked without rewriting originals. The task 0037 timeout and checkpoint-branch decision remain unresolved; the current full-group budget reservation does not fit $40. See notes/results/20261020-verifier-state-hardening.json.
limitations: No new optimizer step or held-out improvement was confirmed at launch.
Context, children, hardware, and infrastructure changed together; this is not a single-variable ablation.
Inference exits before final scoring, audit, and learning; this is not native asynchronous GRPO.
Conservative phase reservations may stop expansion before $40 of literal spend; an idle rental still bills.
experiments.scope_note: RTX continuation within the L1 post-training campaign; paused with verifier and candidate-timeout issues unresolved.

experiments.title: RTX split-card · unchanged eight-rollout baseline
experiments.intent: Before expanding research tools, validate dedicated TP1 inference and one-rank TRL/Muon using unchanged task 0026, checkpoint 17, and rollout protocol.
experiments.change: Used RTX PRO 6000 hardware, explicit two-to-one Muon state conversion, dedicated GPU 1 inference, and GPU 0 verification/learner phases. Root prompt, reward, context, and rollout count did not change.
experiments.conclusion:
Eight rollouts completed, with three correct kernels and no final infrastructure errors.

The exact 39,416-root-token audit passed. All 320 adapters changed in one update, step 17 to 18. Native readback restored all 320 momentum tensors plus scheduler, RNG, and counter. This was one new optimizer point, not 18 new updates.

Collection through readback took 1,137.97 seconds, excluding initial inference startup. The historical L40S task cycle took 2,284.54 seconds, but trajectories and token work differ; this does not establish a repeatable hardware-only speedup or quality gain.
experiments.decision: Control run complete. Do not repeat it or merge this independent branch over the newer L40S policy 19. The expanded child pilot remains separately gated within a $20 total RTX budget.
limitations: Fresh stochastic trajectories were used; samples were not bitwise paired.
Different GPU reference timings affect speed rewards.
Only one update was made; there was no held-out quality evaluation.
Training and verification alternate on GPU 0; this is not a production asynchronous curriculum driver.
experiments.scope_note: Supporting RTX setup/control validation for the L1 post-training campaign, not a cumulative update to the L40S branch.

experiments.title: RTX research pilot · 16K context · compiler children
experiments.intent: Test a larger, bounded research workflow only after resident verification, single-rank resume, the full baseline, and actual child-tool checks pass.
experiments.change: Used 16,384 root context, 4,096 child input and aggregate output limits, and up to two children with two compiler/correctness checks each. Reasoning and root-only loss were preserved. A fenced-source action protocol avoided JSON-escaping CUDA source; format repair used the same token budget.
experiments.conclusion:
Eight rollouts completed: four correct kernels and no final infrastructure errors.

The exact 45,635-root-token audit passed; all 320 adapters changed in one step-17-to-18 update, and native checkpoint readback passed. Cycle time was 1,272.11 seconds, excluding initial inference startup.

All 51 root replies used reasoning; maximum actual context was 11,502, with no length finishes and one turn-limit reply missing its final answer. There were no actual child calls or documentation lookups.

A separate diagnostic child completed 3,560 tokens across four requests, with two format repairs and one correct CUDA check; a failed-compile repair cycle remains unproven.
experiments.decision: The bounded pilot is complete and its checkpoint is backed up. Keep the two-child option: spontaneous use and benefit were not demonstrated. This and the baseline step 18 are separate branches sampled from step 17, not continued L40S coverage or proof of learned improvement. Do not migrate this automatically into the curriculum.
limitations: Several protocol changes were combined; this is not a single-variable ablation.
Tool availability does not prove useful spontaneous delegation.
Both pilot branches start from step 17; their step-18 checkpoints are different models.
The earlier JSON-format diagnostic and zero-sample refused waiter remain preserved.
experiments.scope_note: Independent RTX research pilot supporting the L1 post-training campaign; its step 18 is a separate branch, not cumulative L40S training.

experiments.conclusion:

Training paused naturally at 10:21:59 UTC on task 0006 after three final-verifier workers segfaulted; there was no step 20. CPU inspection found host dereferences of CUDA pointers in those candidates.

experiments.title: L1 continuation · searchable CUDA docs · 10 turns
experiments.intent: Continue preserved policy 8 through unchanged L1 tasks, using searchable archived CUDA guidance and a later submission deadline.
experiments.change: Stored the CUDA 13.3 reference in the REPL; allowed eight normal turns plus two recovery turns, with the first deadline warning at turn eight. Added a focused child example, enabled reasoning, and used CPU precompilation and bounded inference shutdown. Production warm retention stayed disabled.
experiments.conclusion:
Steps 15 and 16 were saved at 06:17 and 06:59 UTC; 16 of 50 tasks were trained. The 16 total updates comprise 11 inherited and five new updates in this run. Eight of the total used the documentation variant.

Both groups submitted all eight candidates, with five correct each. Speeds were 0.977–1.134× for MaxPool3d and 1.093–1.119× for adaptiveMaxPool2d.

The 42,191- and 35,022-token audits passed; both ranks restored fully from 14 to 15 to 16, and all 320 adapters changed at each update. There were no root-admission or final infrastructure errors.

All 92 root replies used reasoning, with no length, capacity, or child outcomes; one recovery was submitted and two documentation searches were used.

The same driver started task 0007 at policy 16. Forty traces and 16 metrics synced; local step-15/16 archives and four file hashes were verified.

The next scoring phase could not fit within the 65-minute bound before 08:00 UTC, so samples were preserved at the guard. No held-out policy improvement is established.
experiments.decision: Training paused naturally at 09:31 Madrid time before task 0007 scoring could fit the October 20 10:00 cutoff. Policy 16 and all eight unscored submissions and the generation manifest are preserved; there was no step 17. The hourly monitor is paused. The original $60 baseline is unchanged and the VM still bills. Child progress and the 4,096-token output cap are CPU-tested source only; they were not deployed in this run. Further training needs renewed time authorization and preserved sampled-protocol provenance.
limitations: Multiple protocol and infrastructure changes are combined; this is not a single-variable ablation.
Forty-two tasks were untrained at launch, including three prior deferrals.
Child outputs remain context only; root reasoning tokens receive GRPO credit but are not replayed in later context.
Inference and learner residency do not overlap. The VM rental continues after workload exit.

experiments.title: L1 curriculum · TRL + Muon · eight rollouts
experiments.intent: Train the pinned Laguna policy with TRL across the unchanged 50-task L1 set in easy-first order, using eight trajectories per task and exact root-only credit.
experiments.change: Used checkpoint-correct rotary settings, constructor-aware CUDA verification, eight trajectories at initial concurrency four, 1,024-token recovery, and phase-shared inference/training on the existing two L40S GPUs.
experiments.conclusion:
Step 8 was saved at 21:33 Madrid time on task 0035; the driver then paused normally at the authorized three-update limit.

One of eight kernels was correct, with reward 0.769 at 0.6875× reference speed (slower). Six submissions completed; there were no final infrastructure errors.

The 49,540-token audit passed; both ranks restored fully from step 7, then changed all 320 adapters.

Eight of 50 tasks have trained updates; 0047, 0019, and 0042 are deferred. Forty trajectories and eight optimizer points synced. No held-out quality improvement is established.
experiments.decision: The authorized block is complete; no additional update or GPU evaluation was launched. Compact checkpoint 8 is independently verified locally, and all deferred samples remain intact. The hourly monitor is paused while Trackio stays available. The VM remains rented and bills when idle; do not stop it without authorization. Post-run repairs and opt-in inference reuse/CPU precompilation are implemented. A zero-update fixed-policy GPU diagnostic measured 66.1 seconds cold versus 2.1 seconds wake, and 99.5 seconds serial versus 69.9 seconds overlapped (29.8% less time); this is not full GRPO throughput. Use a new bounded continuation with explicit scope; the old source/run stays immutable. The old 0038/0041 evaluation pair is not held out; validate a coverage-aware replacement first.
limitations: Eight of 50 tasks have saved updates; 42 remain untrained, including deferred 0047, 0019, and 0042. No held-out quality evaluation is complete.
Task difficulty requires source and constructor values: task 0047 has learned-state contracts but only single-channel 1×1 convolution arithmetic.
Task 0035 had four intermediate GPU-queue timeouts, three length-limited 1,024-token recovery replies, and a recovery-only rule rejection. Final scoring had no infrastructure failure.

Task 0042’s missing final followed recovery-only rule rejections, not token-cap finishes. One child timed out at 90.1 seconds despite a saved backend response at 133.7 seconds; the bridge cancellation repair passes CPU disconnect/admission tests, but live GPU abort and throughput remain unvalidated.
Full distributed learner restore from 7 into 8 passed. Remote and local step 8 passed all four file hashes; earlier backups remain verified. A future distributed restore from 8 remains unobserved.

Post-run repairs and scheduling flags are implemented; fixed-policy GPU component tests passed four CUDA verifications. Full eight-trajectory integration, live child-cancellation latency, and learner/sleeping-server coexistence are not established. The immutable baseline was not hot-patched or restarted.
Trackio uses separate generation, scoring, and one-update trainer runs. A single continuous optimizer-loss curve is not wired.
Reference KL is not computed because beta is zero; missing KL must not be interpreted as zero divergence.
Dollar costs use the displayed rate, not an invoice. The VM continues billing when GPU processes stop.
The registry was refreshed after launch; it is not a new attestation of the immutable source snapshot.

experiments.title: Train exact RLM turns with TRL on two L40S
experiments.intent: Test whether fast tensor-parallel inference can supply genuine CUDA RLM trajectories for a correctly normalized native TRL/Muon update on the same GPU pair.
experiments.change: Used a separate vLLM runtime, exact per-turn prompts and root-only targets, trajectory-level GRPO advantages, native DAPO PPO loss, phase-separated one-step training, and compact adapter export.
experiments.conclusion: A real L1 group produced 22 exact root turns and one native TRL/Muon update. Compact export, CPU readback, and vLLM inference with the trained adapter passed. Rewards were 0.1, 0, 0.1, and 0.1; none of the four kernels was correct. The update carried submission-format signal, not positive correctness or speed signal.
experiments.decision: Keep the TRL/TP2 training route. Fix constructor-state interfaces and verifier feedback delays, then audit sampler/learner clipping before funding a longer run.
limitations: One update or adapter reload does not establish quality improvement.
This run starts from the pinned base, not the earlier Prime checkpoint.
Fresh-process optimizer, scheduler, and sampler resume remain untested.
The native initial clipping statistic was about 0.306, averaged over microbatches and including padding in metrics.
